questions.question_text:
(i) Ravi wants to design a new number system with "0,1,2,3,4,5" as the basic digits . Help him in
(a) Finding the base for his new number system (1mark)
(b) Generating the first 20 numbers in that number system (2 marks)
(c) Convert the decimal number 20 to the new number system (1 marks)
(ii) convert 67.687 to binary number system (3 marks)
(iii) convert 111011.1101 to decimal number system (3 Marks)
questions.answer:
(i) Analysis of Ravi's number system with digits "0,1,2,3,4,5":
(a) **Base for the new number system**: Since there are 6 unique symbols (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), the base (or radix) of this number system is **6** (Senary number system).

(b) **First 20 numbers in base 6 (starting from 0)**:
0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 30, 31

(c) **Convert decimal 20 to base 6**:
- $20 \div 6 = 3$ remainder $2$
- $3 \div 6 = 0$ remainder $3$
Reading remainders bottom-up gives $(20)_{10} = (32)_6$

(ii) **Convert 67.687 to binary number system**:
- **Integer Part (67)**:
  - $67 \div 2 = 33$ rem 1
  - $33 \div 2 = 16$ rem 1
  - $16 \div 2 = 8$ rem 0
  - $8 \div 2 = 4$ rem 0
  - $4 \div 2 = 2$ rem 0
  - $2 \div 2 = 1$ rem 0
  - $1 \div 2 = 0$ rem 1
  - Integer part in binary = $1000011_2$
- **Fractional Part (0.687)**:
  - $0.687 \times 2 = 1.374$ (integer: 1)
  - $0.374 \times 2 = 0.748$ (integer: 0)
  - $0.748 \times 2 = 1.496$ (integer: 1)
  - $0.496 \times 2 = 0.992$ (integer: 0)
  - $0.992 \times 2 = 1.984$ (integer: 1)
  - $0.984 \times 2 = 1.968$ (integer: 1)
  - Fractional part in binary $\approx 0.101011_2$
- **Total converted binary value** $\approx 1000011.101011_2$

(iii) **Convert 111011.1101 to decimal number system**:
- **Integer Part ($111011_2$)**:
  $1 \times 2^5 + 1 \times 2^4 + 1 \times 2^3 + 0 \times 2^2 + 1 \times 2^1 + 1 \times 2^0 = 32 + 16 + 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 59$
- **Fractional Part ($.1101_2$)**:
  $1 \times 2^{-1} + 1 \times 2^{-2} + 0 \times 2^{-3} + 1 \times 2^{-4} = 0.5 + 0.25 + 0 + 0.0625 = 0.8125$
- **Total decimal value** = $59 + 0.8125 = 59.8125$

questions.question_text:
(i) Find the product of the given decimal number 15.75 and 14.25 and the result in binary number system (5 marks)
(ii) Perform division on 18.5 by 6 in the binary number system (5 marks)
questions.answer:
(i) **Product of 15.75 and 14.25 in binary**:
- Convert both decimal numbers to binary:
  - $15.75_{10} = 15_{10} + 0.75_{10} = 1111.11_2$
  - $14.25_{10} = 14_{10} + 0.25_{10} = 1110.01_2$
- Perform binary multiplication:
  ```
           1111.11   (15.75)
         x 1110.01   (14.25)
         -----------
           111111
          0000000 
         00000000  
        111111000   
       1111110000    
      11111100000     
      -------------
     11100000.0111_2
  ```
- **Verification**: $11100000.0111_2 = 128 + 64 + 32 + 0.25 + 0.125 + 0.0625 = 224.4375_{10}$. Indeed, $15.75 \times 14.25 = 224.4375$.

(ii) **Division of 18.5 by 6 in binary**:
- Convert both decimal numbers to binary:
  - $18.5_{10} = 10010.1_2$
  - $6_{10} = 110_2$
- To simplify division, shift the binary point to make the divisor an integer. Thus, $10010.1 \div 110$ is computed as $100101 \div 1100$ (shifting point 1 position right in both numbers):
- Perform binary division:
  ```
                 11.000101...
           __________________
     1100 | 100101.000000
          -  1100
          -------
             01101
            - 1100
            ------
              0001.0 (remainder 1, bring down 0)
                     (continue division after point)
  ```
- The resulting binary quotient is $11.0001010101..._2$, which equates to $3.08333..._{10}$ ($18.5 \div 6$).

questions.question_text:
(i)Add the following BCD numbers 237.75 and 486.25. (5 marks)
(ii)Subtract the following BCD numbers 275.5 from 422.25. (5 marks)
questions.answer:
(i) **BCD Addition of 237.75 and 486.25**:
- Convert the decimal digits directly to BCD form:
  - $237.75 \rightarrow 0010\ 0011\ 0111\ .\ 0111\ 0101$
  - $486.25 \rightarrow 0100\ 1000\ 0110\ .\ 0010\ 0101$
- Add the BCD representations column-wise from right to left, adjusting each group if the sum exceeds 9 (add $0110_2$ to correct):
  - **Hundredths**: $0101 + 0101 = 1010_2$ ($10 > 9$). Add $0110_2$ correction:
    $1010 + 0110 = 10000_2 \rightarrow$ result **$0000$** with carry-out of $1$.
  - **Tenths**: $0111 + 0010 + 1 \text{ (carry)} = 1010_2$ ($10 > 9$). Add $0110_2$ correction:
    $1010 + 0110 = 10000_2 \rightarrow$ result **$0000$** with carry-out of $1$.
  - **Units**: $0111 + 0110 + 1 \text{ (carry)} = 1110_2$ ($14 > 9$). Add $0110_2$ correction:
    $1110 + 0110 = 10100_2 \rightarrow$ result **$0100$** with carry-out of $1$.
  - **Tens**: $0011 + 1000 + 1 \text{ (carry)} = 1100_2$ ($12 > 9$). Add $0110_2$ correction:
    $1100 + 0110 = 10010_2 \rightarrow$ result **$0010$** with carry-out of $1$.
  - **Hundreds**: $0010 + 0100 + 1 \text{ (carry)} = 0111_2$ ($7 \le 9$). No correction needed:
    result **$0111$** with no carry.
- Combined BCD output: $0111\ 0010\ 0100\ .\ 0000\ 0000$ which represents **$724.00$**.

(ii) **BCD Subtraction: $422.25 - 275.50$ using 10's complement**:
- Represent $275.50$ as a 5-digit number: $275.50$
- Find 9's complement of $275.50$: $999.99 - 275.50 = 724.49$
- Add $1$ to find 10's complement: $724.49 + 0.01 = 724.50$
- Add the minuend ($422.25$) and 10's complement of the subtrahend ($724.50$) in BCD:
  - $422.25 \rightarrow 0100\ 0010\ 0010\ .\ 0010\ 0101$
  - $724.50 \rightarrow 0111\ 0010\ 0100\ .\ 0101\ 0000$
  - Perform addition:
    - **Hundredths**: $0101 + 0000 = 0101_2$ (**5**, no correction)
    - **Tenths**: $0010 + 0101 = 0111_2$ (**7**, no correction)
    - **Units**: $0010 + 0100 = 0110_2$ (**6**, no correction)
    - **Tens**: $0010 + 0010 = 0100_2$ (**4**, no correction)
    - **Hundreds**: $0100 + 0111 = 1011_2$ ($11 > 9$). Add $0110_2$ correction:
      $1011 + 0110 = 10001_2 \rightarrow$ result **$0001$** with end-around carry-out of $1$.
- The carry-out of $1$ signifies a positive result. Discarding the carry yields: $0001\ 0100\ 0110\ .\ 0111\ 0101$ which represents **$146.75$**.

questions.question_text:
(i) Differentiate the following statements (4 marks)
(a) ADD A,B,C
(b) ADD A,B
(c) ADD A
(d) ADD
(ii) A system has 64 GB of memory and is word addressable. The size of each word is 16 bytes. Find the size of the address bus for this system. (3 marks)
(iii) Describe Index addressing with suitable example. (3 marks)
questions.answer:
(i) **Differentiation of instruction address formats**:
- **(a) ADD A, B, C (Three-Address Instruction)**: Contains three explicit address fields (two source operands, one destination operand). 
  - Operation: $A \leftarrow B + C$ (Computes sum of elements at addresses $B$ and $C$, stores result in address $A$).
- **(b) ADD A, B (Two-Address Instruction)**: Contains two explicit address fields (one acts as source-only, and the other as both source and destination).
  - Operation: $A \leftarrow A + B$ (Adds values at $A$ and $B$, overwrites $A$ with result).
- **(c) ADD A (One-Address Instruction)**: Specifies only one address field. It implicitly utilizes an Accumulator ($AC$) register for the other operand and destination.
  - Operation: $AC \leftarrow AC + M[A]$ (Adds the memory value at address $A$ to register $AC$, storing result in $AC$).
- **(d) ADD (Zero-Address Instruction)**: Contains zero explicit addresses. This is used in stack architectures where operands are implicitly taken from the top of the stack.
  - Operation: Pop top two elements, add them, and push the sum back onto the top of stack ($TOS \leftarrow TOS + NOS$).

(ii) **Finding Address Bus Size**:
- Given:
  - Memory Size = $64\text{ GB} = 64 \times 2^{30}\text{ bytes} = 2^{36}\text{ bytes}$
  - Word size = $16\text{ bytes} = 2^4\text{ bytes}$
- Since the system is **word-addressable**, each address refers to a single word of memory.
- Number of addressable word locations = $\frac{\text{Memory Size}}{\text{Word Size}} = \frac{2^{36}}{2^4} = 2^{32}$ locations.
- Therefore, size of the address bus = $\log_2(2^{32}) =$ **$32\text{ bits}$**.

(iii) **Index Addressing Mode**:
- **Definition**: In index addressing mode, the Effective Address ($EA$) of the operand is obtained by adding a constant displacement/offset to the contents of an index register ($IX$).
  - Formula: $EA = A + [IX]$ (where $A$ is the base address value given in instruction, and $[IX]$ is index value).
- **Example**: 
  - Let index register $IX = 2000$.
  - An instruction `LOAD R1, 50(IX)` is executed.
  - Base displacement $A = 50$.
  - $EA = 50 + 2000 = 2050$.
  - The operand is retrieved from memory address $2050$ and loaded into register $R1$.
- **Application**: Useful for accessing arrays and sequential data structures, as iteration can be done simply by incrementing register $IX$.

questions.question_text: With a neat sketch, describe the architecture of 8086 microprocessor.
questions.answer:
### Architecture of 8086 Microprocessor

The Intel 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor with a 20-bit address bus (enabling up to 1 MB of memory addressing space) and a 16-bit data bus. 

Its structural architecture is uniquely divided into two functional units working in parallel, allowing overlapping instruction fetching and execution (pipelining):

#### 1. Bus Interface Unit (BIU)
The BIU handles all data and address transfers between the processor, memory, and I/O devices.
- **Segment Registers**: Memory is split into logical segments of 64KB each. The segment registers contain the base addresses: 
  - **CS (Code Segment)**, **DS (Data Segment)**, **SS (Stack Segment)**, **ES (Extra Segment)**.
- **Instruction Pointer (IP)**: Points to the offset address of the next instruction code in memory.
- **Address Generator Circuit**: Automatically computes the 20-bit physical memory address using the segment base and offset offset: $\text{Physical Address} = (\text{Segment Address} \times 10\text{H}) + \text{Offset Address}$.
- **6-Byte Instruction Queue**: Enables instruction prefetching. The BIU pre-fetches up to 6 instruction bytes while the EU is decoding and executing previous instructions, improving system throughput.

#### 2. Execution Unit (EU)
The EU is responsible for decoding and executing the instruction stream.
- **Instruction Decoder**: Decodes instructions fetched from the BIU queue.
- **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)**: Operates arithmetic/logical instructions on 8-bit or 16-bit registers.
- **General-Purpose Registers**: 
  - Data Registers: **AX** (Accumulator), **BX** (Base), **CX** (Count), **DX** (Data). These can be used as individual 8-bit registers (AH, AL, BH, BL, etc.).
  - Pointer/Index Registers: **SP** (Stack Pointer), **BP** (Base Pointer), **SI** (Source Index), **DI (Destination Index)**.
- **Flags Register**: A 16-bit register holding 9 active flag bits (6 Status Flags: Carry, Parity, Auxiliary Carry, Zero, Sign, Overflow, and 3 Control Flags: Trap, Interrupt, Direction).

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         8086 MICROPROCESSOR                             |
+---------------------------------------+---------------------------------+
|          BUS INTERFACE UNIT           |         EXECUTION UNIT          |
|                                       |                                 |
|   +-------------+                     |   +-------------------------+   |
|   |   Segment   |                     |   | General-Purpose Regs    |   |
|   |  Registers  |                     |   |  AX, BX, CX, DX         |   |
|   | CS,DS,SS,ES |                     |   |                         |   |
|   +------+------+                     |   | Index/Pointer Regs      |   |
|          |                            |   |  SP, BP, SI, DI         |   |
|   +------v------+                     |   +------------+------------+   |
|   | 20-bit Addr |                     |                |                |
|   | Generator   |                     |   +------------v------------+   |
|   +------+------+                     |   |   Instruction Decoder   |   |
|          |                            |   +------------+------------+   |
|   +------v------+                     |                |                |
|   | Instruction |                     |   +------------v------------+   |
|   | Queue (6 B) |======(Pipeline)====>|   | Arithmetic Logic Unit   |   |
|   +-------------+                     |   |        (ALU)            |   |
|                                       |   +------------+------------+   |
|                                       |                |                |
|                                       |   +------------v------------+   |
|                                       |   |      Flag Register      |   |
|                                       |   +-------------------------+   |
+---------------------------------------+---------------------------------+
```
